CFItems.fullStatement: Career Coaching
Can apply understanding of Coaching Principles (adapted from ICF Competencies)
Can establish and sustain a productive career coaching relationship
Demonstrates respect and trust
Demonstrates intercultural awareness
Knows how to deal with differences and negotiating conflict
Knows how to use labor market information sources.
Can integrate and apply a competency-based approach to identify employer needs and labor market expectations.
Knows how to access and use the O*NET Online Database
Knows how to identify available and appropriate skilling and educational opportunities for a participant
Knows how to use and apply tools to clarify participant needs, skills, and interests
Can help clients identify goals, skills, needs, and career interests using competency-based tools
Knows how to use and apply tools to clarify career participant goals and identify career pathways
Knows how to use and apply tools to identify available jobs/careers
Knows how to help a client navigate the job application process using resume, application, cover letter, and interview
Demonstrates understanding of the role of assessments
Use assessment tools to inform a competency-based hiring process
Can interpret assessment results for a client
Can communicate assessment results to clients
Demonstrates the ability to be an active listener
Demonstrate effective interpersonal communication skills
Demonstrates the ability to ask powerful questions
Demonstrates the ability to communicate directly and effectively
Partnerships
Demonstrates understanding of core principles of collective impact as the foundational organizing theory for building a coalition to advance a sector initiative
Can apply collective impact principles to facilitate regional sector initiative(s)
Understand the role of key stakeholders within the local workforce development landscape including the Backbone Agency and Sector Facilitators
Can identify the key drivers and necessary stakeholders to advance a regional sector initiative
Understand the key motivations and drivers of a sector initiative including dual customer approach and talent-supply demand and hiring
Can develop strategies and frameworks that organize the sector initiative to best serve non-traditional career seekers
Can develop strategies and frameworks to facilitate sector initiatives

Demonstrates understanding of the basics of the WIOA funding including outline of the four titles of the WIOA and importance of assigning clients to a distinct working group to identify and secure funding
Can coordinate resources and wraparound services to support regional sector initiatives and the individuals they benefit
Can identify initiative costs, including start-up, system maintenance, program development, and incremental participant costs

Demonstrates ability to identify funding options that leverage a braided funding strategy by identify local funds applicable to each of the components of the career pathways system and determine resource gaps to seek additional funding to fill the gaps
Can identify the three dimensions of organizing the sector initiative: 1. Leadership Council; 2. Working Groups; and 3. Project Teams
Can foster opportunities to partner with stakeholders and customers
Demonstrates understanding of the role of the Sector Facilitator to organize the Leadership Council and establish agreements on the vision, strategy and tactics
Demonstrates ability to work with Leadership Council to establish a shared vision, mission, goals, and strategies for governing the partnership
Demonstrates ability to create work plans for working groups
Demonstrates understanding of talent supply-demand data and employer priorities
Demonstrates understanding of employer signals and can clearly define hiring requirements
Demonstrates understanding of how to build regional talent supply chain
Demonstrates understanding of how to provide evidence-based career coaching
Demonstrates understanding of how to provide evidence-based career profiles
Demonstrates understanding of how to source funding to increase job related education and training
Analysis
Can identify the components needed to make evidence-based decisions at a regional level
Can identify the assets needed to begin a regional analysis
Demonstrates understanding of why data is necessary and vital to a successful regional analysis
Demonstrates understanding of differences between the region-wide system and individual data points/stakeholders
Can leverage assets to facilitate analysis and alignment of employer needs with regional supply
Demonstrates understanding of the O*NET Online Database
Demonstrates understanding of how and why the supply side is fragmented
Demonstrates understanding of how to leverage available resources to align supply and demand
Can select partners, convene subject matter experts, and Identify necessary labor market information channels to choose high-value projects
Can explain the job analysis process and principles of competency-based sourcing and hiring
Can use the O*NET to obtain necessary information
Can create O*NET-based Job Families
Can describe the contents of a Job Analysis report
Demonstrates understanding of how Talent Acquisition can use reports and assessments to create evidence-based selection systems
Can communicate the uses of the job analysis report and LMI data to stakeholders and how to apply it within their work
Can describe how HR can use job analysis to improve job descriptions and Structured Interviews
Can explain how job analysis can inform evidence-based career coaching
Can describe how job analysis reports indicate transferable skills
Can explain how consortia-style job analysis can improve Employer Advisory Groups (EAGs) and curriculum development
Leadership
Can analyze what leadership looks like in your setting
Can use domain knowledge to inform interactions with various stakeholder groups
Can evaluate your domain knowledge needed in order to interact with your stakeholders
Can create an action plan for developing domain knowledge to support interactions with various stakeholder groups
Can identify different stakeholder types in your work

Can inspire stakeholders to develop and
implement solutions to problems
Can analyze the motivation of the stakeholders
Can compare and contrast strategies to motivate stakeholders to develop solutions to problems across systems
Can facilitate communication among diverse groups and interests to create alignment
Can develop techniques to facilitate meetings with stakeholders to achieve a common purpose
Can develop a plan to facilitate a meeting in which you need to resolve a problem
Can analyze elements of reasoning (purpose, questions, information, concepts, inferences, assumptions, implications and points of view) applicable to critical thinking
Can explain how critical thinking skills inform decision-making and problem solving
Can evaluate a common challenge using elements of reason as criteria for evaluation
Can develop a plan to motivate stakeholders to develop solutions to problems that incorporate elements of reasoning
Can identify the needs and values of stakeholder audience groups
Can shift from formal structured message passage to a shared understanding and relationship building through communication
Can design messages relevant to a community and/or system
Can identify the best means for communicating with different audiences/stakeholders
Can compare and select communication strategies
